question: For delivered orders, how much higher is the average review score of on-time orders than late orders (on-time average minus late average)? Late means delivered after the estimated delivery date; ignore orders without a delivery date.
sql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        r.review_score,
        o.order_delivered_customer_date,
        o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 
            ELSE 0 
        END AS is_late
    FROM orders o
    JOIN reviews r ON r.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
      AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
    AVG(CASE WHEN is_late = 0 THEN review_score END) -
    AVG(CASE WHEN is_late = 1 THEN review_score END) AS avg_score_diff
FROM delivered
